title: Implement authenticated GraphQL artifact-transfer tickets
description:
Purpose: Add the server-authorized transfer plane for large artifacts.

Owned scope:
- Add createArtifactTransferTickets to the Amplify GraphQL schema.
- Add its resolver, storage permissions, and canonical key policy.
- Accept Cognito and workload IAM identities, never public API keys.
- Validate resource existence, ownership boundary, artifact type, filename, content type, size, and SHA-256.
- Return five-minute signed HTTPS transfers in batches of at most twenty.
- Enforce a 100 MiB write limit and prevent caller-selected buckets or paths.

Acceptance:
- Contract tests cover typed validation, authorization rejection, canonical keys, batching, methods, headers, and expiry.
- The operation is additive and deployable before any consumer migration.
- No client-specific information or public transfer capability is introduced.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Milestone: implemented the additive createArtifactTransferTickets mutation and resolver. It accepts one to twenty typed READ/WRITE requests; derives canonical keys server-side for dataset, procedure, score-result, and task artifacts; validates filename, media type, nonnegative size, lowercase SHA-256, resource existence, trusted-account consistency, and the 100 MiB write cap. Tickets expire after five minutes and return objectKey, method, url, requiredHeaders, and expiresAt. The mutation allows Cognito and IAM identity-pool authorization only; API keys are excluded. Resolver IAM is scoped to DynamoDB GetItem and canonical object prefixes only. Focused resolver and schema/infra contract suites pass (11 tests); schema generation/check and resolver TypeScript compile pass. Risk/follow-up: current deployment has no universal Plexus account-membership claim for every identity. The resolver fails closed when a trusted account claim/context is present and otherwise relies on the existing authenticated AppSync boundary while deriving the referenced resource account server-side. Membership rearchitecture is intentionally outside this lane.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Compatibility follow-up complete: GraphQL now requires operation, resourceType, and artifactType fields. Dataset keys preserve the account-scoped canonical layout . SHA-256 input is normalized case-insensitively before signing to interoperate with the shared artifact store. Safe nested relative filenames are supported for task artifacts while traversal and unsafe path segments are rejected. To preserve existing dashboard-state pointers, PROCEDURE_DASHBOARD_STATE explicitly maps to ; its IAM scope is limited to that legacy prefix. Added behavior coverage for all four cases; focused suites now pass 14 tests.
